props.title: A Woman Under the Influence
props.initialSlug: Love can break what reality can't bend

sections.content: A Woman Under the Influence (1974) stands as John Cassavetes' raw masterpiece of psychological realism. Gena Rowlands delivers a shattering performance as Mabel Longhetti, a working-class housewife whose erratic behavior and mental instability strain her marriage to Nick (Peter Falk). Cassavetes' signature improvisational style and intimate handheld camerawork create an almost documentary-like intensity that influenced later character studies like Blue Valentine (2010) and Martha Marcy May Marlene (2011). The film's unflinching portrayal of mental illness broke new ground in American cinema, paving the way for works like One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975).

sections.content: The film's influence on depicting mental health in cinema cannot be overstated. While Hollywood often sensationalized mental illness, Cassavetes showed it through a deeply human lens. This approach echoes through later works like Clean, Shaven (1993) and Silver Linings Playbook (2012), though few match its uncompromising vision. Rowlands' performance particularly influenced actresses like Julianne Moore in Safe (1995) and Elisabeth Moss in Queen of Earth (2015).

The film's exploration of working-class domestic life set new standards for American independent cinema. Its influence can be seen in the works of directors like Kelly Reichardt, particularly Wendy and Lucy (2008), and Sean Baker's The Florida Project (2017). The raw emotional authenticity and focus on marginalized characters created a template for contemporary social realism. SUBHEAD: Impact on Independent Filmmaking

sections.content: Cassavetes' guerrilla filmmaking approach - self-financing, using family and friends as crew, shooting in real locations - established a blueprint for American independent cinema. Directors like Jim Jarmusch with Stranger Than Paradise (1984) and Harmony Korine with Julien Donkey-Boy (1999) directly borrowed from his methods. The film's success proved audiences would embrace challenging, character-driven narratives outside studio conventions.
